name: SUMAC
label: Thrill Jockey
lede: Aaron Turner wanted the heaviest music of his life, got a drummer by way of Kurt Ballou, and spent the next decade pulling his own riffs apart to make room for improvisation.

eras.title: Heavier than a bag of hammers
eras.text: Four years after Isis ended, Aaron Turner was on Vashon Island in Puget Sound, running the SIGE label with his wife Faith Coloccia and writing riffs he meant to be the heaviest he'd made. He needed a drummer who could keep up. Noisey's first headline on the band: heavier than a bag of hammers.

years.big: "I've never been in a band that sounds like this"
years.h: Kurt Ballou hands Aaron Turner a drummer
years.p: [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]'s [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]], who produced [[Baptists|d00125a6-a009-4171-8cc5-9837620ec200]]' Bloodmines, points Turner to that band's Vancouver drummer, Nick Yacyshyn. They jam in Vancouver, then Yacyshyn goes to Turner's place on Vashon.
years.xp:
That's Yacyshyn, talking to Exclaim! in November 2014. He called the music "a pretty dense, heavy experience and kind of out there," and said the pair didn't take other rock bands as models.

Turner insisted it was a full-time band that would write, record and tour, not a side project.

years.h: Russian Circles' Brian Cook is hired for one album and stays
years.p: Exclaim! announces SUMAC with [[Brian Cook|e5915350-afd0-405b-a461-f9c9420f9509]], also of [[Botch|72448406-ba82-43a7-9e13-d9a47ff333f4]], on bass. He was brought in to play on the debut and quickly became a full member.
years.xp: Yacyshyn hadn't met him yet. "I've never met Brian before," he told Exclaim!. "I'd love to meet him and have a jam, just the three of us."

years.h: Two jams in, SUMAC open for Deafheaven in Vancouver
years.p: The band's first show, in December 2014, is a support slot for [[Deafheaven|f4ccf6c5-ad41-4f8f-bb9e-6e2c6ad23302]]. Per Wikipedia, they had only rehearsed twice.

years.h: Rolling Stone premieres 'Blight's End Angel' with Grohl in the headline
years.p: The headline calls Nick Yacyshyn [[Dave Grohl|4d5f891d-9bce-45ae-ad86-912dd27252fa]]'s favorite new drummer, a few weeks before the album is out.

years.cap: SUMAC opening for Neurosis, St. Vitus Bar, Brooklyn, c. 2015
years.p: SUMAC's six-song debut, recorded in Seattle by Mell Dettmer ([[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]], [[Earth|60dd41cf-8f9d-46d8-bc19-dc7e5acb24c8]]) and mastered by Kurt Ballou in Salem, Massachusetts. Turner's SIGE label handles the vinyl.
years.xp: Profound Lore put it out on February 17, 2015, after 'Thorn in the Lion's Paw' and 'Blight's End Angel' had gone out as previews. A short North American tour followed in March, including a Vancouver show in Yacyshyn's hometown.

eras.title: Thrill Jockey, and an unrehearsed week in Tokyo
eras.text: Thrill Jockey put SUMAC next to experimental rock instead of metal, and the band used the room. Kurt Ballou recorded the albums. Unrehearsed sessions in Tokyo with the Japanese noise musician Keiji Haino changed how they wrote.

years.p: Exclaim! reports the Chicago label has signed the band for its second album, five months before it comes out.

years.cap: SUMAC at Great Scott, Allston, Massachusetts, August 20, 2016
years.h: What One Becomes turns anxiety into five long tracks
years.p: Kurt Ballou records SUMAC's second album. Turner wrote about his own struggles with anxiety and what happens when an identity comes apart.
years.xp: The album came out on Thrill Jockey on June 10, 2016, four months after the signing.

years.h: Four remixers take What One Becomes apart
years.p: Kevin Drumm, [[Endon|92e57202-8ca1-4a5a-9cd9-320a1787de0a]], Samuel Kerridge and Bleed Turquoise rework material from the album on a four-track EP.

years.big: a series of unrehearsed, completely non-premeditated sessions
years.h: SUMAC and Keiji Haino walk into a Tokyo studio with no plan
years.p: Summer 2017, Goksound, Tokyo. Thrill Jockey's description of the recording with Haino, the Japanese noise musician.
years.xp: The sessions became American Dollar Bill – Keep Facing Sideways, You're Too Hideous to Look at Face On. Thrill Jockey credits them with pushing improvisation into SUMAC's own records from then on. Two more albums with Haino followed.

years.h: Two hundred cassettes of SUMAC on WFMU
years.p: SIGE releases WFMU Live, a session recorded for Brian Turner's show on the New Jersey freeform station, limited to 200 copies.

years.cap: SUMAC at National Sawdust, Brooklyn, c. 2018
years.h: The Tokyo sessions with Haino come out as American Dollar Bill
years.p: Thrill Jockey releases the first SUMAC and Keiji Haino album, recorded at Goksound the summer before.

yt: Live at the Regent Theater, Los Angeles, January 2018
years.h: Four songs, five days, over an hour: Love in Shadow
years.p: SUMAC record live at Robert Lang Studios in Shoreline, Washington, with Kurt Ballou. Turner wanted to write about love in its spiritual, vulnerable sense, and its corrupted forms.
years.xp:
Turner's statement: "Love has been well worn theme throughout a lot of rock music, but most commonly in terms of love-lost." The album is about "what some of the repercussions are for love that is scorned, suppressed or socially discouraged."

Minimal overdubs, by design: the band wanted a human presence on tape. Turner said fitting "free and open space" inside the songs had been an ongoing goal, and credited the Haino collaboration.

eras.title: Held, healed, filmed
eras.text: More Haino albums, and SUMAC records that got longer and looser. Turner's lyrics turned to fatherhood and a society he saw coming apart. In 2025 the band gave the microphone to Moor Mother.

years.h: Haino and SUMAC go again, on Trost
years.p: The second album by SUMAC and Keiji Haino comes out on Trost Records, on CD in June 2019 and vinyl in July.

years.h: SUMAC put out Two Beasts on Sub Pop and a St. Vitus set on SIGE
years.p: Two Beasts comes through Sub Pop. St Vitus 09/07/2018 is a live set from the Brooklyn club.

years.cap: Turner, Cook and Yacyshyn, press photo, c. 2020
years.h: May You Be Held is stitched together from three studios
years.p: Kurt Ballou in Shoreline, Matt Bayles in Anacortes, and Turner's House of Low Culture on Vashon Island. Turner wrote about fatherhood and a society in upheaval.
years.xp:
Turner on the record: "As an artist in this time of significant upheaval, society seemingly having reached the end of its current iteration, it's of critical importance to absorb and interpret this process of dissolution."

He described his vocals as "wounded, primal, and mammalian," and the record as one that "feels more human than anything else." It opens on improvised guitar drones and vibraphone and closes on a quiet improvisation.

years.h: Haino and SUMAC make it three
years.p: Into This Juvenile Apocalypse Our Golden Blood to Pour Let Us Never is the third SUMAC and Keiji Haino album, on Thrill Jockey.

yt: Live at Rubber Gloves, Denton, August 9, 2024
years.h: The Healer runs 76 minutes over four tracks
years.p: SUMAC's fifth studio album, Thrill Jockey catalog number 609, is about wounds as a way to growth. The Keeper's Tongue EP followed the same year.

years.h: Moor Mother turns a SUMAC double album into The Film
years.p: Recorded with Scott Evans at Studio Litho in Seattle, with singers Kyle Kidd, Sovie and Candice Hoyes. Turner painted the art.
years.xp:
Moor Mother on the plan: "The idea is to create a moment outside of the convention. This is a work of art. Thinking about the work as a Film, instead of an album or a collection of songs."

Her list of themes: "land - displacement - the climate - human rights and freedoms - war and peace."
